title: Researching learned optical fields
description: Neural field prediction is an AIFIELD research direction. It asks whether a trained model can estimate field behavior in specified conditions; it does not replace the classical solver capabilities described elsewhere.
lead: Neural field prediction is an AIFIELD research direction. It asks whether a trained model can estimate field behavior in specified conditions; it does not replace the classical solver capabilities described elsewhere.

sections.heading: The experiment framing
body: A model receives a description of a photonic problem and boundary information, then predicts an optical field. Comparison with classical calculations can reveal where the estimate resembles or departs from the reference under the tested conditions.

sections.heading: Limits of the current evidence
body: The reviewed results depend on supplied boundary information. From-scratch prediction, larger stitched domains and a practical speed advantage remain open questions. The available summary does not supply a general benchmark with conditions and figures appropriate for a public performance claim.

sections.heading: A useful next study
body: Further work should define training and test separation, geometry and boundary families, error measures, failure cases, compute cost and comparison conditions. These details would make a claim about generalization or engineering usefulness assessable.
